Teach me the CSS box model from beginner to advanced.

**CSS box model — Beginner to Expert**

[Beginner]
Every element is a box: content, padding, border, margin, from inside out.
```css
.box { width: 200px; padding: 16px; border: 2px solid #333; margin: 8px; }
```
Why it works: width sizes the content area; padding, border and margin are added around it.

[Intermediate]
Set `box-sizing: border-box` globally so declared width includes padding and border.
```css
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
```
Why it works: with `border-box`, `width: 200px` really renders 200px total, ending arithmetic surprises.

[Advanced]
Manage margin collapse: it happens between vertical margins of adjacent/parent-child blocks; prefer `gap` in flex/grid containers.
```css
.stack { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; }
```
Why it works: gap is real space on the container, so it never collapses with child margins.

[Expert]
Use logical properties (`margin-block`, `padding-inline`) and `inset` shorthand for direction-aware boxes.
```css
.notice { padding-block: .75rem; padding-inline: 1rem; margin-block-end: 1rem; }
```
Why it works: logical properties follow the writing direction, so RTL layouts need no overrides.

Debug: I positioned a badge with position:absolute and top/right, but it anchors to the page corner instead of the card it is inside. Why?

**Symptom:** an absolutely-positioned element ignores its visual parent and snaps to the corner of the page or of some distant ancestor. **Root cause:** `position: absolute` positions against the nearest ancestor whose position is NOT `static` — not necessarily the DOM parent. If the card is `position: static` (the default), the badge climbs the tree until it finds a positioned ancestor, often ``. ```html
3
``` ```css /* BROKEN */ .badge { position: absolute; top: -8px; right: -8px; } /* FIXED: make the intended parent the containing block */ .card { position: relative; } .badge { position: absolute; top: -8px; right: -8px; } ``` Any of these on an ancestor ALSO creates the containing block: `absolute`, `fixed`, `sticky`, plus `transform`, `filter`, `will-change` or `contain: layout`. **Diagnosis:** in DevTools, select the badge, then temporarily give suspicious ancestors `outline: 1px solid red` while nudging `top/right` — you will see which box it actually measures against. The Computed panel shows each ancestor's `position`. **Fix:** add `position: relative` to the intended parent (it changes nothing else visually). **Prevention:** pair every `position: absolute` child with an explicit `position: relative` on its wrapper as a habit, and remember `transform`/`filter` also capture absolute children — check ancestors before blaming the CSS.

«async/await» را از مبتدی تا پیشرفته به من یاد بده.

## [مبتدی]
A promise is a placeholder for a future value; .then() chains consume it.

## [متوسط]
async/await is syntax sugar: await pauses the async function until the promise settles, making code read top-to-bottom.

## [پیشرفته]
Wrap awaits in try/catch and check response.ok — fetch does NOT throw on HTTP 404/500.

## [حرفه‌ای]

I need two font families on one page. What is the most efficient way to request them from Google Fonts?

```html
<!-- One CSS request carries both families and all weights -->
<link rel='preconnect' href='https://fonts.googleapis.com'>
<link rel='preconnect' href='https://fonts.gstatic.com' crossorigin>
<link href='https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;600&display=swap' rel='stylesheet'>
```

```css
body { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; }
pre, code { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; }
```

Why it works: multiple family parameters in a single css2 URL produce one CSS response that declares both families, so the browser makes one request for the stylesheet instead of two. The .woff2 files themselves are still fetched individually per family/weight, but only when a weight is actually used on the page. Efficiency checklist: combine families in one URL, list only weights you use, add display=swap, preconnect to both hosts, and give every family a matching fallback keyword (sans-serif, monospace) so text renders even if the network fails.

لطفاً margin collapsing را با مثال توضیح بده

Adjacent vertical margins between block siblings collapse into the larger of the two; a parent with no border/padding also collapses with its first/last child's margin. Flex/grid items never collapse — switching the parent to display:flow-root or flex stops it.

```css
.container { display: flow-root; /* contains child margins */ }
```

Debug: My flexbox container is not centering its items even though I wrote display:flex. What am I doing wrong?

**Symptom:** `display: flex` is set, but items hug the top-left corner or only center on one axis. **Diagnosis:** flex centering needs BOTH axis properties, and several things silently defeat it: ```html
Center me
``` ```css /* BROKEN: no height — a block div is content-sized, so there is no vertical space to center within */ .wrap { display: flex; align-items: center; } /* FIXED: give the container a size and set BOTH axes */ .wrap { display: flex; justify-content: center; /* main axis (horizontal in the default row) */ align-items: center; /* cross axis (vertical) */ height: 100vh; /* or 100% of a sized parent */ } ``` Other silent killers — check in DevTools: - A typo like `display: flexbox` or the rule overridden by a stronger selector (shown struck-through in the Styles panel). - The child has `position: absolute`, which removes it from flex flow — center it relative to its positioned parent instead. - `flex-direction: column` swaps the axes: `justify-content` becomes vertical. - The container itself has collapsed width (e.g., it is an inline element or an unsized flex item). **Fix:** confirm the computed style really shows `display: flex`, set both `justify-content` and `align-items`, and make sure the container actually has height/width to center within. **Prevention:** keep the one-liner `display: flex; place-items: center;` (shorthand for both axes) together with an explicit size on the container; for centering a single child, `margin: auto` on the child inside a flex container also works.

HTML معنایی (Semantic HTML) یعنی چه و چه عناصر معنایی مهمی وجود دارد؟

HTML معنایی یعنی انتخاب عنصری که معنی محتوا را بیان کند، نه فقط شکل ظاهری آن. مهم‌ترین عناصر معنایی:

- `header`: سربرگ صفحه یا بخش
- `nav`: مجموعه لینک‌های ناوبری
- `main`: محتوای اصلی و یکتای صفحه (فقط یکی در هر صفحه)
- `article`: محتوای مستقل مثل پست و خبر
- `section`: گروه موضوعی با عنوان
- `aside`: محتوای جانبی مثل ستون کنار
- `footer`: پاورقی صفحه یا بخش
- `figure` و `figcaption`: تصویر یا نمودار با توضیح

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="fa" dir="rtl">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>نمونه ساختار معنایی</title>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Vazirmatn:wght@400;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  <style>
    body { font-family: "Vazirmatn", sans-serif; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <header>سربرگ سایت</header>
  <nav>منوی ناوبری</nav>
  <main>
    <article>محتوای اصلی</article>
    <aside>ستون کنار</aside>
  </main>
  <footer>پاورقی سایت</footer>
</body>
</html>
```
